comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological claims (C2-C4, C66-C82). Both evaluations rate the VP system development and experimental methodology as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes technical parameters and ethical approvals, while peer reviewers praise the approach as 'novel and exciting' and 'an impressive feat.'

Perfect agreement on behavioral validation claims (C19-C21). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on statistical validation and above-chance performance, while peer reviewers emphasize the VP's ability to 'dynamically vary its synchronization' and achieve 'high degree of experimental control.'

Strong agreement on network engagement claims (C22-C26, C40). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses 6 claims including C40, peer review addresses 7 claims including C5. Both affirm engagement of dorsal/ventral pathways across frequency bands, with peer reviewers noting the study 'helps to elucidate some of the brain areas involved in interactive speaking behaviours.'

Strong agreement on spatial clustering and correlation findings (C27-C31, C41). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes silhouette scoring and frequency-dependent correlation reversal, while peer review (covering C6-C7, C27-C31, C41) highlights the distinction between behavior-related and global task activity as a key contribution.

Strong agreement on auditory cortex differential sensitivity (C32-C35). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes C7 and emphasizes the gradient along dorsal pathway with FDR corrections, while peer reviewers affirm the distinction between primary and secondary auditory cortex as demonstrating 'different brain regions' with different sensitivities.

Divergent evaluations on right hemisphere findings (C36-C37, C8-C10). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about sparse coverage (C10), while peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting the 'limitation' of 'relatively sparse coverage of the right hemisphere' affecting statistical power and interpretation confidence.

Partial overlap on IFG engagement (C8-C9). OpenEval result R6 covers C36-C37, C8-C10 rated SUPPORTED with coverage caveats. Peer result R6 covers C8-C9, C42 rated SUPPORTED, explicitly recognizing 'bilateral IFG as a potential candidate supporting verbal coordination' without expressing the same level of concern about right hemisphere coverage.

Agreement on phase-amplitude coupling findings (C38-C39). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers C38-C39, C42, C60 and notes the IFG coupling with coordination dynamics as novel, though C60 interpretation is 'somewhat speculative.' Peer review covers only C38-C39, affirming PAC findings as part of the study's contribution using SEEG's temporal resolution.

Minimal overlap on claim C42. OpenEval R7 includes C42 as part of PAC analysis rated SUPPORTED. Peer R6 includes C42 with IFG findings (C8-C9) rated SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers accepting the interpretation of IFG activity showing 'phase-amplitude coupling relationship.'

Divergent evaluations on prediction error interpretation (C45-C48). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C45 is data-supported but C46-C48 are 'explicitly speculative interpretations' requiring additional validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the prediction error framework as part of the theoretical contribution providing 'convincing evidence.'

Divergent evaluations on right STG interpretation (C49-C51). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the reconciliation via temporal/spectral specialization is 'interpretive' and limited by sparse right hemisphere coverage. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with concerns about 'relatively sparse coverage of the right hemisphere' directly affecting confidence in right hemisphere function claims.

Agreement on Broca's area continuous dynamics interpretation (C52-C58). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the interpretation is 'well-reasoned' though C57 is 'somewhat speculative.' Peer reviewers affirm the contribution to understanding IFG function and praise the study for going 'beyond previous work' with continuous dynamics representing 'a significant advance.'

Agreement on theoretical integration (C59, C61-C62). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R11 covers C59, C61-C65 emphasizing integration with predictive coding and anatomical connectivity. Peer R12 covers C59-C62, accepting theoretical interpretations as part of understanding 'unfolding temporal dynamics of brain-behaviour relationships.'

Partial overlap on anatomical connectivity claims (C63-C65). OpenEval R11 includes these as part of theoretical contextualization rated SUPPORTED. Peer R13 includes these among broader background claims (C1, C11-C18, C43-C44, C63-C65) rated SUPPORTED, affirming the study's positioning within the field.

Perfect agreement on signal processing methods (C83-C87). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the appropriateness of bipolar montage, artifact rejection, and frequency band definitions. Peer reviewers praise the SEEG methodology for providing 'spatial and temporal resolution necessary' with no concerns about signal processing.

Strong agreement on background and context claims (C1, C11-C18). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R13 covers C1, C5-C6, C11-C18 emphasizing literature support and gap identification. Peer R13 covers C1, C11-C18, C43-C44, C63-C65, affirming the study 'goes beyond previous work' and addresses an 'understudied area.'

Minimal overlap on prior literature claims (C43-C44). OpenEval R14 covers only C43-C44 rated SUPPORTED as accurately summarizing prior literature. Peer R13 includes C43-C44 among broader background claims rated SUPPORTED, accepting them as appropriate context.

Minimal overlap on claim C60. OpenEval R7 includes C60 as part of PAC interpretation, noting it is 'somewhat speculative' though plausible, overall rated SUPPORTED. Peer R12 includes C60 among theoretical interpretations (C59-C62) rated SUPPORTED, accepting it as part of the study's theoretical contribution.
